quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: When I saw the news, the first thing comes to mind is, as us all, we want to know what happened, right? First thing first, condolences, prayers go out to his family. You just want to know what happened, 29 years old. It's very seldom, I don't think it ever really happened with me while I was playing in the NBA that we had someone passed away. Moments like this always make you reflect and be grateful for the people that you do have. It makes you realize that you should value people a lot more, especially your loved ones, your friends, your family. Over the last six, seven months, I lost both my grandmothers. I lost my great aunt right before Mother's Day. You just never know when your time is called to go home. It's almost shocking in a way when you hear a 29-year-old young man like Brandon Clark passed away. It's just unfortunate, but it's life. My biggest thing is to approach each day with a positive mindset, and it doesn't hurt to be nice.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins reflects on the sudden death of Brandon Clark, emphasizing the fragility of life and the importance of valuing loved ones, a sentiment resonating deeply within the NBA community.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: They snatch your fucking soul defensively. I'm not going to even speak on the whole offensive end. I could care less about the flopping. I'm going to appreciate what I've been witnessing from them defensively from top to bottom. SGA, always the league leader in steals, best player, not a defensive liability. Then seeing him block ducks, shots, all type of shit. Then you move to Alex Caruso, who's just this pit bull that's caged up on the bench and is like sic 'em. He comes in and brings a whole different type of tenacity. I've never seen a team full of two-way players like this in my life. It is not one single guy that you could look at on that roster and say that he is a defensive liability. Not one. They have at least five to six guys that you could put as an All-Defensive on an All-Defensive team, if not more.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins praises the Oklahoma City Thunder's exceptional defense and roster full of two-way players, highlighting their unique team dynamic and defensive prowess.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: AJ Mitchell, he's the only person I'm going to address offensively. God bless America. Do you all realize that this dude is on basically playing on a vet minimum contract? He signed a three-year deal for $8 million. Sam Presti is out here finessing the shit out of people. A three-year deal for about $8.2 million. They have him under contract for the next two years. He is making, I believe, next year he'll be making $2 million.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins points out the incredibly team-friendly contract of AJ Mitchell, crediting Sam Presti's front office for their shrewd financial management.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: This team is on a damn mission. Young guys who don't give a damn about individual accolades. It's all about them winning championships. Coach Dago said after I want to say game two, where Jalen McCan went off, he makes business decisions on whether he's going to play Jalen McCan minutes or Andrew Wiggins. He told a story how those guys are their each other's biggest supporters. If one is in the game and the other one is not getting minutes, it drew them closer together. You don't find shit like that in today's game.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins highlights the Oklahoma City Thunder's unique team-first mentality and strong player support, attributing it to Coach Dago's effective leadership.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.quote: Sometimes you got to remove something to make room for the plants that you want to grow. I think what OKC does, they are very the way they communicate with their players through the GM, through the owner, through the vision is why they're all bought in. This team is the new version of San Antonio. San Antonio back in the day with Tim Duncan, they had their big three, which is Jalen, JDub, SGA, and Chet. Out of that, everyone else is not replaceable, but they have somebody that is right behind them ready to take that position. Lou Dort goes down, I got somebody for you. Jalen Williams goes down, I got somebody else for you. That's been waiting that believes in this system that knows that Sam Presti is going to take care of them. So AC, you're not doing so well this game? Here, I got somebody else for you behind you. They don't take that personally because they know when their time is up, he's going to take care of them and move them to where they need to get moved to get paid.
quotes.why_it_matters: Frye praises the Oklahoma City Thunder's organizational communication and player buy-in, comparing their system to the successful San Antonio Spurs model of developing and managing talent.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.quote: I think showing people, showing your team that you are that guy and that you are trustworthy and that your communication is on level 12, that guys are bought in for the $2 million. Because at the end of the day, AJ Mitchell is going to get paid. They win another championship, he does well, they're going to say AJ Mitchell, you know what we're going to do? We're either going to pay you ourselves for time spent and reward you for your time here, or we're going to find someone else where you not only can you play, but you're going to get the money that you may have missed by allowing us to pay these guys so that we can win championships. That is rare in this league. It is rare. But if you have great communication, you show people you're about your business like Sam Presti has, right? He got Chet, SGA, and JDub all to sign contracts where the salary cap is going up. So their contracts won't hamper so that they can pay everyone else on the team and they can continue to be good. So it's the organization, it's their culture. I think when you talk about just on the court, everyone is so bought in. There's not a thought of myself, it's a thought of what is my role, what is my job within this this time and in the and my time on the court.
quotes.why_it_matters: Frye elaborates on Sam Presti's strategy of securing team-friendly contracts for star players, ensuring financial flexibility to retain and reward other talent, fostering a strong team culture.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.quote: You talk about the empowerment from player to player and wanting everyone to succeed and just, you know, teammate to teammate. I find that to be so fascinating, large in part because it's such a young group still, despite some of the vets that they have. I know, Perk, because you understand the organization and you have been in there, that you'll be able to understand what I'm saying with this. Mark Dago was asked about his approach to his team and the MO that he kind of carries. I thought this was fascinating. He said the best advice he's received is simple: be there when they need you. Early on, that meant more guidance and direction, but now it's not over-coaching or taking away their ownership. He actually thinks that that's the worst thing you can do. I think that that is something that he has found a balance of so well, but it can be said too, not just for the coaching staff, but the front office. And you know, the other night, Rui was asked, how are you able to muster up the belief in getting a game in the series period? And he was talking about just how every player, no matter who it is, understands their role. When you can see that from the outside looking in, it just they they put themselves in a completely different category.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clifton highlights Coach Dago's philosophy of empowering players and fostering a strong team dynamic, where every player understands their role without being over-coached.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: Those guys go to practice, go to their families, on the video game, and go their ass back to the gym, and then go their ass to the arena. You got to have a different mentality. Everybody doesn't fit that system. It's just a different type of mentality and a different type of will that you got to have, and if you don't accept it, then you won't be there for long. Jalen McCan said it himself, 'I was sad as hell when I got traded from Philly, but when I got there, I was like, oh shit, yes, it's a real fucking culture.' We'll probably never hear about not one of OKC Thunder players being involved in something at a nightclub, being involved somewhere they're not supposed to be. Those guys go to practice, go to their families, on the video game, and go their ass back to the gym, and then go their ass to the arena. You got to have a different mentality. Everybody doesn't fit that system. It's just a different type of mentality and a different type of will that you got to have, and if you don't accept it, then you won't be there for long.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins emphasizes the unique and disciplined culture of the Oklahoma City Thunder, where players are expected to be fully committed to the team's values both on and off the court.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: The Knicks are legit title contenders. They could win it all. The way that they're clicking on both sides of the basketball, they could win it all. Here's why I say they're the biggest threat. In order to beat OKC, number one, you have to get their defense moving side to side, and you have to get those guys in rotation. Mike Brown has adjusted his offense. By the way, he's unlocked a different fucking version of Karl-Anthony Towns, and I love it. He has unlocked a different version of Karl-Anthony Towns with that offense, point center. There's so much movement that's happening. In order to beat the Thunder, you have to make three-point shots. The Knicks are making three-point shots at the highest level. McBride, Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, Jordan Clarkson, OG Anunoby, Karl-Anthony Towns, they are shooting it. In order to beat because what what OKC is great at, there's no driving gaps. They're going to take away driving gaps, they got active hands, they're getting deflections. They go do late contested tough three-point shots and put them in rotations. The Knicks could really beat the Thunder. I'm not saying the Spurs or Minnesota wouldn't have a chance, but if I had to pick my favorite out of the three, I would go with the New York Knicks.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins identifies the New York Knicks as the biggest threat to the Oklahoma City Thunder, citing their strong 3-point shooting and offensive adjustments as key factors to counter OKC's defense.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.quote: The convenience of it works out for LeBron, but I don't think this is a championship contending team. I think they have some other very serious glaring holes that they need to address. So if I'm LeBron, I'll say, hey, I'll come back. I just need to see what you bring back. They need a new center. Let's see who you go get. As in seeing what they bring back for the roster. If I'm LeBron, I'll say, hey, I'll come back. I just need to see what you bring back. They need a new center. That's it. I mean, let's see who you go get.
quotes.why_it_matters: Frye expresses skepticism about the Lakers' championship contention, suggesting LeBron's return hinges on the team addressing significant roster deficiencies, particularly at the center position.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: They need a new makeover. It's not just DeAndre Ayton, which by the way, I think he has a player option for his second year if I'm not mistaken, or is it guaranteed? Whatever it is, he better take that because if he don't take that or if he's not guaranteed, he won't be in the league. He's on his he's on his last straw. It's a rap for him if he don't get his shit together. If if if the Lakers don't decide to waive him. I would bring back Marcus Smart. Player option for the second year. Oh, he's taking that. He's he's definitely taking that. He better. He better. He better or he's going to find his ass back in the Bahamas because nobody's going to want to take a chance on him. Channing, what? Somebody's going to take a chance on him. Who? There's not that many seven-foot centers. You were the same one that said he didn't serve a purpose. I just said he's a master of nothing. That's what I said. Which is true. Because his inconsistency shows that you can't rely on him to do one thing night in and night out. This is the truth.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins delivers a harsh assessment of DeAndre Ayton's career, stating he's on his 'last straw' and needs to accept his player option or risk being out of the league due to inconsistency.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.quote: No. He's not. He's not. Yes, he would. He's spent eight and a half years. Channing, I'm not saying he shouldn't deserve one. I'm saying he's not going to get one. Channing, he better get a statue there at Crypto.com Arena. They don't accept him. Lakers fans don't accept him. It's great. He's had better careers just in the Lakers than most other players. If we if we really want to look around. They just don't accept him. Magic Johnson, James Worthy, Jeanie Buss, make the shit happen. Fuck what y'all talking about. Fuck what the Lakers nation don't accept and all that shit. LeBron has spent eight years in that playing for the Lakers. NBA championship, Finals MVP, breaking all type of fucking records. Scoring records at at that. Imagine being in a Lakers uniform and passing up Kobe on the all-time scoring list. Then passing up Kareem on the all-time scoring list. Then hitting fucking 40,000 in a Lakers uniform. No, bro. That man deserves a fucking statue in front of Crypto.com Arena.
quotes.why_it_matters: Perkins passionately argues that LeBron James unequivocally deserves a statue at Crypto.com Arena, citing his eight years with the Lakers, championship, Finals MVP, and record-breaking scoring achievements.
